    What the crew does

      Request help — water damage ☎ (718) 487-9596

      Insurance documentation

      Your claim is only as strong as your documentation

      Adjusters approve what they can verify. From the first visit, the damage is documented the way an insurance file needs it — so the scope of work is provable, not argued.

      1

      Document before anything moves

      Photos and video of the damage, the source, and everything affected — captured before cleanup or demolition begins, while the evidence is intact.

      2

      Measure, don't guess

      Moisture readings and a room-by-room scope record how far water, soot, or mold actually traveled — including the damage you can't see behind walls.

      3

      Build the claim file

      The photos, readings, and scope are assembled into one organized file you can hand to your insurer and adjuster — nothing reconstructed from memory weeks later.

      4

      Restore to the documented scope

      Repairs and remodeling follow the same documented scope, so the finished work and the claim tell the same story.
